fatal_errors: The proposed tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy is unrelated to the target ZrB2–30% AlFeNiCoCr cermet and omits the critical 1500 °C spark-plasma-sintering intervention.
Neither cited paper tests resistance to molten aluminum: E1 concerns mechanical strength, while E2 concerns high-temperature oxidation in an oxidizing atmosphere.
High melting point and oxidation resistance do not establish chemical inertness or resistance to dissolution and intermetallic formation in molten aluminum.
The proposed material and coating composition are insufficiently specified to permit reproducible fabrication or meaningful interpretation of the corrosion test.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the same broad engineering problem—protecting hot-dip-aluminum equipment—but does not reconstruct the demonstrated material, processing optimum, structural mediator, or quantitative performance. The target is a ZrB2 cermet with an equimolar AlFeNiCoCr binder, optimized by SPS at 1500 °C; its performance arises from binder-assisted pore filling, high density, and strong ZrB2 grain bonding. The generated answer instead proposes an unspecified tungsten RHEA whose coherent nanoprecipitates are documented for strength but not for molten-aluminum compatibility. Its cited oxidation evidence is not transferable to immersion corrosion in liquid aluminum. The proposed comparative immersion experiment is directionally useful and falsifiable, but it needs a defined alloy/coating process, appropriate target-relevant controls, dimensional or thickness-loss corrosion measurements, cross-sectional penetration/reaction-layer analysis, and testing near 700 °C for comparable durations. Thus, it is a novel but presently unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target result.
